system.name: Tempo
system.one_liner: a deep learning system that compiles a declarative, recurrent-tensor program into a whole-program-optimized schedule via a symbolic dependence graph

content.subject: how Tempo augments the symbolic dependence graph with new nodes for tensor deallocation and for GPU-CPU memory swapping

elements.name: SDG
elements.role: dashed boundary marking the original, unaugmented symbolic dependence graph containing C and P

elements.name: C
elements.role: the consumer node, with domain Omega_C, that reads a tensor produced by P

elements.name: P
elements.role: the producer node, with domain Omega_P, whose tensor C consumes

elements.name: Dealloc
elements.role: panel (a) only: new node that frees P's tensor once both production and C's last use have happened

elements.name: Evict_B
elements.role: panel (b) only: new node that evicts the reloaded tensor back to CPU after C's last use

elements.name: Load
elements.role: panel (b) only: new node that reloads P's tensor from CPU back to GPU for C to consume

elements.name: Evict_A
elements.role: panel (b) only: new node that evicts P's tensor to CPU immediately after production

relations.what: the consumer C reads tensor P via mapping phi, unchanged inside the SDG
Dealloc has an identity dependence on P: it may only run after P produces its tensor
Dealloc also depends on C via the inverse mapping phi^-1, so it waits until C has finished consuming that timestep's tensor
in the swap augmentation, C's dependency on P is redirected through phi to Load instead
Load has an identity dependence on Evict_A; the evicted copy must exist before it can be loaded back
Evict_A has an identity dependence on P, evicting P's tensor to CPU memory right after it is produced
Evict_B depends on C via the inverse mapping phi^-1, so the second eviction waits until C's last use

content.key_idea: Memory management operations (deallocation, or GPU/CPU swap eviction and reload) are added to the SDG with an identity dependence on producer P and an inverse-mapped dependence on consumer C, so they run only after production and last use.
content.reading_order: in (a) Deallocation, C and P inside the SDG box, then Dealloc below with its two dependence arrows; in (b) Swap, the same pair plus Evict_B above and Load/Evict_A below

palette.used_for: pale cream fill of the dashed SDG background box
white fill of every node circle

style.stroke: thin black circle outlines; dashed black border around the SDG sub-box
style.arrows: thin black arrows labelled phi or phi^-1 (or left unlabelled for an identity dependence) linking each new node to C and/or P
style.font: italic serif math notation (C, P, Omega, phi) inside plain sans-serif circles; bold sans-serif 'SDG' and panel captions

encoding.color_means: purely monochrome; the only fill distinction is the pale cream dashed box marking which nodes belong to the original, unaugmented SDG versus the new memory-management nodes drawn outside it
encoding.line_style_means: a dashed border separates the original SDG (C, P) from the newly added nodes; solid arrows labelled phi or phi^-1 (or left unlabelled for a plain identity dependence) show each new dependence
encoding.state_means: not applicable; both panels are single static augmented graphs, not before/after states of one graph
encoding.emphasis: keeping C and P inside a visually distinct dashed 'SDG' box while drawing every new memory-management node outside it makes clear that augmentation only adds dependencies, never touches the original computation graph
reusable_patterns: a small unchanged sub-graph ringed by a dashed boundary, with new operator nodes attached outside it by labelled forward/inverse dependency arrows
weaknesses: phi and phi^-1 look nearly identical at this size (an inverse-exponent superscript), so a reader must look closely to see which direction of dependency each arrow encodes

sections: §5 Scheduling SDGs with the Polyhedral Model
evidence: Fig. 15a shows how Tempo augments the SDG with deallocations for the tensor produced by P and consumed by C
Deallocation must always happen after production, which Tempo models with an identity dependence
Fig. 15b shows how Tempo augments the SDG with evict (GPU-to-CPU) and load (CPU-to-GPU) memory movement operations

summary: Figure 15 shows two ways Tempo augments a symbolic dependence graph (SDG) with memory-management nodes, keeping the original producer P and consumer C (linked by phi) inside a dashed SDG box in both cases. In (a) Deallocation, a Dealloc node is added outside the SDG with an identity dependence on P (it may only run after P is produced) and an inverse-mapped (phi^-1) dependence on C (it must wait for C's last use of that timestep) before deallocating P's tensor. In (b) Swap, C's dependence on P is redirected through phi to a new Load node, which itself depends on an EvictA node that evicts P's tensor to CPU right after production; a further EvictB node, depending on C via phi^-1, evicts the reloaded copy again once C is done with it, completing a GPU-to-CPU-to-GPU round trip.
summary_zh: 该图示Tempo为SDG添加内存节点：P、C(经φ相连)仍在虚线框内；(a)新增Dealloc，待P产出且C末次使用后才释放；(b)C改依赖新增Load，其依赖EvictA(产出即逐出CPU)，EvictB依赖C用完后再逐出，完成往返。
